shots.caption: mind — a local attention manager
shots.narration: Your attention is spread across mail, a calendar, pull requests, and a phone. mind gives back the part that is just triage.

shots.caption: One machine · one server · one SQLite file
shots.narration: It runs on one machine: one server, one SQLite file, one process. The server is the single source of truth; the editor and the phone are clients. You write Directions — rules for how a kind of signal should be handled. mind matches signals against them, drafts when a reply is needed, and leaves only the real decisions in a Queue. A thought appears only where there is ambiguity or consequence. Nothing is sent until you approve it.

shots.caption: One link per section
shots.narration: The VS Code extension is the main client. The mind icon opens a deliberately thin sidebar: one link per section, no live data until you open one.

shots.caption: Goals on the left, waiting work on the right
shots.narration: On the left, your goals. On the right, everything waiting without one. Each item says when it needs you and why. Drag an item onto a goal to link it; new items link themselves when the model is confident.

shots.caption: Transcript, Audio, Details
shots.narration: Transcript gives you the day in text. Audio reads exactly that text aloud, rendered on this machine with Piper. Details opens the conversation, the thought, and the history.

shots.caption: Approval is the only send
shots.narration: Approve a draft, and that is the only place a send is authorised. Discard closes it without sending. Nothing leaves the machine until you choose one of these.

shots.caption: Signals — reclassify anything misrouted
shots.narration: Signals lists every signal, inbound and outbound, today by default. If one matched the wrong Direction, reclassify it here.

shots.caption: Directions are the rules
shots.narration: Directions is the rule table. Open a row to edit its standard and its prompts, and Preview dry-runs the saved rule against stored signals.

shots.caption: Learnings — proposals from your overrides
shots.narration: Learnings shows the policy proposals the learning loop generates from your own overrides.

shots.caption: Coverage: absorbed signals vs. Directions in force
shots.narration: Analytics puts the coverage curve first: how much is absorbed each week against the number of Directions in force. Click a week to see the signals behind it.

shots.caption: Each client gets its own scoped credential
shots.narration: Devices is where a second client pairs. Name it, choose its permissions, and show a six-digit code.

shots.caption: Not a second inbox
shots.narration: The Android client is not a second inbox. It pairs with that code.

shots.caption: Read and capture, on the phone
shots.narration: With read and capture it can show the Queue, capture a thought, acknowledge a signal, and keep the last queue on the device.

shots.caption: Approve and discard need send
shots.narration: Approve and discard appear only when the device was granted send.

shots.caption: Offline, labelled stale
shots.narration: Cut the server and the cached queue stays, labelled stale. Revoke the device and it is locked out on its next request.

shots.caption: BSD-3-Clause · local-first
shots.narration: One operator, one machine, BSD-3-Clause, local Ollama. Not a notification system or a cloud service — just the few decisions that need a person.
